# Romakajātaka (Ja 277)

**ID:** Ja 277
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Romakajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Pigeon

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Romakajātaka* (Ja 277), also attested in manuscript traditions under the title *Pārāpatajātaka*, is a birth-story located in the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1879; Fausböll 1897]. According to its commentary, the Buddha delivered the story while residing at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) near Rājagaha concerning an attempt on his life [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the past, set in Bārāṇasī during the reign of King Brahmadatta, the Bodhisatta was born as the leader of a flock of pigeons nesting in a mountain cave near a hermitage [Fausböll 1879]. After a virtuous ascetic departs, a hypocritical ascetic arrives who conceals a desire to trap and feast on the birds; perceiving his murderous intentions, the Bodhisatta utters the verses rebuking him, alerts the flock, and leads them to safety in another gorge [Fausböll 1879]. In the identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the treacherous ascetic was Devadatta, the former virtuous hermit was Sāriputta, and the pigeon king was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1879].

Episodes from the *Romakajātaka* are depicted in Kushan-period Buddhist relief art on the railing pillars at Mathurā [Dutt 1956; Chauley 1998].

SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages but lists no canonical parallels in other Buddhist traditions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language matches above threshold, but records four Pali-internal text-reuse matches with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), covering the canonical verses (§1.1–2.4) embedded in the commentary [DharmaNexus].
